accuracy.evidence: Alliteration is defined as the repetition of the same initial sound in words close together, matching Letters and Sounds Phase 1 Aspect 5 (DfES 2007) and the Oxford English Dictionary sense. Every first sound was checked by ear and against standard UK and US pronunciations: /s/ sun, sock, seal; /m/ moon, mouse, milk, mop; /b/ bun, bat, ball, bus, bear, bouncy; /k/ kite, cake, key, cat, coat; /g/ goat, gate; /tʃ/ cheese; /ʃ/ shoe; /f/ fish, fork, fluffy, funny; /d/ dog, duck, door, dizzy, dish; /l/ log, leaf, little; /h/ house. Odd-one-out decoys were checked to rhyme with a set member (sun/bun, mouse/house, bat/cat, dog/log) but not share its first sound. The adult text says alliteration is judged by ear and describes pure sounds without overclaiming that it causes later reading success.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the confusions documented in early phonological awareness research (Carroll, Snowling, Hulme and Stevenson 2003; Treiman and Zukowski 1991) and Letters and Sounds Phase 1 guidance: rhyme taken for a shared start (bun, house, cat, log in step 2, p1, m1, m2, challenge 'rhyme'), letters over sound (cake and cat written with c in step 3, cheese starting with c but /tʃ/, p3, challenge 'spell'), a sound at the end counted as the start (bus, leaf in step 5, p5, m9, challenge 'end'), meaning over sound (sock and shoe in step 5, m3, challenge 'mean'), and close voiced/unvoiced sounds (goat in step 3, m4, challenge 'close').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagallit is about hearing and matching the first sound by ear: two sound bags (sss, mmm), an odd-one-out where the odd word rhymes with a set member, a starts-like-kite board with letter and close-sound decoys, alliterative phrase building, and same-start versus end-sound pair judgements. flagrhyme judges end sounds, flagphon links letters to sounds and flagrime builds onset and rime from letter tiles; none uses rhyme as a trap or end-sound pair judging. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule before the text gives it: a card dropped in the wrong bag says its first sound slowly, bun is the odd one out with feedback saying it rhymes but starts differently, goat is turned away with a k-versus-g explanation and cake is accepted with a note that the sound is k though the letter is c, wrong phrase words name both first sounds, and leaf and bus are judged 'not the same' with the reason that the sound is at the end. Tapped words are spoken where the device has speech, so it is an ear task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Yes, they sound alike' for sun and bun (bun is the odd one out), 'No, the letters are different' for kite and cake (cake is accepted as starting like kite), and 'Yes, both have fff' for fish and leaf (leaf is judged not the same start).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with one of six messages: rhyme is the end not the start, listen not look (letters), the sound is at the end, meaning is not sound, close sounds (k and g), and a general first-sound reminder. Answer order rotates between questions.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and one-syllable words, with the sounds written as they are said (sss, mmm); the adult text names Letters and Sounds Phase 1 Aspect 5, Development Matters, CCSS RF.K.2.d and key terms (initial sound, phoneme, phonological awareness). The lab uses the young layout with big picture cards and buttons, and every task word is spoken on tap. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: the shared first sound, rhyme versus start, ears not eyes and start not end, and alliterative phrases. Items cover choosing a matching start (p1, p4, m1, m4), letters vs sound (p3), end sound (p5, m9), odd one out (m2, m8), meaning trap (m3), the definition (m6), phrases (m7) and counting (p2, m5).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and desktop light screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me (wn-run-1117-1553). At 360 px the two bags sit side by side with names above the animal, six picture cards fit a 3 by 2 grid, the kite board fits five cards in two rows, phrase chips are at least 44 px tall and the Same start / Not the same answer buttons are at least 54 px tall. Bag labels were moved above the animal after the first screenshot showed 'Mmm monkey' crowding the monkey.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: put each picture in either bag, pick the odd one, ask whether each word starts like kite, put each describing word before the animal, and judge each pair as same start or not. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the first sounds involved. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
